window-1.title: laurel.world — Laurel Schwulst's site
window-1.blurb: It's less a portfolio than a soft cream-colored room you wander through, where every project links sideways to another by year, medium, or friend — the kind of hand-made web object that'll make you want to rebuild your own site by midnight.

window-2.title: Charlotte Rohde's new typeface has heart-dotted i's and a plan to overwrite problematic men
window-2.blurb: A typeface designed as a full character — heart-dotted i's, a feminist bit committed all the way to the end, and a launch campaign shot to look like a photocopier running out of toner — which is exactly the kind of type-as-persona nonsense you'd stay up all night making yourself.

window-3.title: Non-Alcoholic Espresso Stout Martini
window-3.blurb: A zero-proof espresso martini crossed with a stout — dark, foamy, absurdly photogenic in a coupe, and exactly the kind of committed-to-the-bit drink you'd hand someone at 10pm just to watch their face.

window-4.title: The Selby — Inside Creative People's Homes
window-4.blurb: It's basically permission to let your rooms look like your brain — every shelf, taped photo and inherited lamp doing the decorating for you.
